<reason>A more convincingly distinguished useful conservation incentives from the primary safeguard for essential reserves. Its pool-ban comparison undermined B's opening fairness claim, while its pressure questions exposed B's reliance on assuming strong price responsiveness and deteriorating restriction enforcement. Neither policy guarantees sufficient savings, but A acknowledged that uncertainty more honestly. B offered plausible recurring incentives and administrative advantages without adequately resolving what happens when heavy users keep paying while withdrawals overshoot.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's strongest rebuttal was that tariffs can miss the water target even with perfect compliance because paying is compliance. This punctured B's “budget with a dial” framing without claiming restrictions enforce themselves. B answered by asserting that a sufficiently sharp price would collapse outdoor demand, leaving the challenged assumption largely intact.</best_rebuttal>
